title: Expectation of Finite Sums
statement: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces, with strictly positive coordinate weights summing to $1$. For any finite set $s$ and any family of real-valued functions $F_i$ on the product outcome space, the expectation of their sum over $s$ equals the sum of their expectations: $\mathbb E_P[\sum_{i\in s}F_i]=\sum_{i\in s}\mathbb E_PF_i$.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite product probability space
All coordinate weights are strictly positive and sum to $1$
Each $F_i$ is real-valued on the product outcome space
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, a finite index set $s$, and functions $F_j:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\mathbb E_P\sum_{j\in s}F_j=\sum_{j\in s}\mathbb E_PF_j$.
